question: Does the 2018 PSFBE Marikina River fish-survey abstract provide a usable species-level or station-level checklist?
citation: Gilles, A. S., Jr., Arbasto, P. D. U., Arnaldo, C. A. S., Corpuz, C. J. S., Sidhu, R. K., & Pavia, R. T. B. (2018). An alien river: Non-native fish species dominate a heavily impacted Philippine river. Abstract in the proceedings of the 2nd Philippine Symposium on Freshwater Biodiversity and Ecosystems (PSFBE 2018).

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the society-hosted proceedings PDF's indexed abstract text on 2026-11-19. A direct PDF open was rejected because the file exceeded the browser fetch size limit; no local copy was retained. The PSFS event page identifies the meeting as the 2nd PSFBE in December 2018 and says copies of the abstract book can be requested from its secretariat. UP Diliman independently confirms the symposium dates as December 11-14, 2018.
sourceAccess.licenseFinding: No item-specific open license or permission to reuse the abstract, data, or images was identified. Only concise findings and source metadata are recorded.

abstractFindings.studyPeriod: Not stated in the reviewed abstract.
abstractFindings.localityTextAsPrinted: Apia, Antipolo, Rizal M.H. del Pilar Street, Rodriguez Rizal, San Mateo, Rizal, Barangay Tumana in Marikina, and Marikina Riverbanks.
abstractFindings.localityInterpretation: The abstract says five sites but its punctuation does not unambiguously map the printed locality phrase to five distinct site names. Preserve the phrase as printed; do not geocode or assign the five-site total to inferred locations.
abstractFindings.nativeStatusStatement: The abstract says almost all surveyed species were non-native, except a few that may have been introduced during pre-Hispanic times. It names none of the species and provides no taxon-level evidence in the abstract.

evidenceDecision.decision: Accept as a dated retrieval lead for a historical Marikina River survey, not as a species checklist.
evidenceDecision.reason: The abstract reports aggregate counts and general methods only. It does not name the 14 taxa, give a station-by-species table, or specify collection dates, vouchers, coordinates, or unambiguous site mapping. Its historical narrative cannot establish present-day occurrence or taxon-level origin.

nonClaims: The reported total of 14 species is not a recoverable species list and cannot be used to create 14 species records.
The abstract's non-native narrative does not identify which taxa it refers to and does not support species-level invasive or native labels.
The five-site count and the printed locality phrase do not establish a validated site-to-waterbody crosswalk or river geometry.
The abstract does not establish current presence, absence, catchability, fishing access, legal harvest, safety, or diet guidance.
nextActions: Seek the full PSFBE 2018 abstract book or any associated paper with a named species list and station-specific methods through lawful public or author/institution access.
If a full list is located, preserve original spellings and independently review taxonomy, locality mapping, survey dates, vouchers, and item-specific reuse terms before any species projection.
Continue NCR freshwater, brackish, marine, and waterbody-denominator research; keep the NCR baseline and Luzon phase incomplete.
